summary: This release uses stock OMP v18.10.2 as its engineering baseline. The 2 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.7.6. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
highlights:
- This release uses stock OMP v18.10.2 as its engineering baseline. The 2 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.7.6. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
- Classify a timed-out 1Password identity probe as a host fault with the macOS installed-path recovery recipe. Kill an unresponsive probe at its 30-second deadline, distinguish external signals from timeouts, and preserve the release driver's explicit new-candidate retry gate.
- Move the OMP engineering baseline to published v18.10.2 (#398), with pins derived by `scripts/upstream-pins.ts`. Registry v1, the discovery file format, the relay protocol, `collab.autoStart`, and the collaboration `host.ts`, `settings.ts`, and `collab-web` sources are unchanged from v18.8.9. The registry moves onto native IPC with the same request and response lines and relocates overlong sockets under `/tmp/omp-<euid>` (can1357/oh-my-pi@a608a9ca07); host relay pings (can1357/oh-my-pi#14387) and `ctx.annotations` (can1357/oh-my-pi#15260) change nothing the gateway reads or sends. The embedded client remains at v18.4.2. No qualification is claimed; published v0.7.6 stays bound to OMP v18.8.9.

- Classify a timed-out 1Password identity probe as a host fault with the macOS installed-path recovery recipe. Kill an unresponsive probe at its 30-second deadline, distinguish external signals from timeouts, and preserve the release driver's explicit new-candidate retry gate.

- Qualify stock OMP v18.10.2 on every host lane. Requalify all thirteen lanes, including session-lifecycle and Push-triage scenarios, on these exact signed bytes; historical receipts and canaries do not transfer.
plannedBoundary: - Planned qualification: Debian 13 x86-64; macOS 27.0 (26A428) arm64 in a Virtualization.framework guest (VirtualMac2,1, ADR-033); a disposable Windows Server 2025 host (the Administrator lifecycle and a fresh standard-user install); Chrome on the physical Pixel 10 Pro, including its background-Push lane; and real iPhone, iPad, and Galaxy devices in TestingBot's cloud. Every lane must pass against these exact signed bytes before stable promotion; the plan is not evidence.
candidateRollback: The selected predecessor is v0.7.6; pruning keeps it installed as the recorded rollback target. Gateway rollback does not switch or restart OMP. Historical fork-era recovery is documented separately in docs/UPGRADE_ROLLBACK.md.
